senses.sense_definition: A specific level or rank within an organization, society, or professional hierarchy.

examples.text: The company's top <w>echelon</w> decided to change the entire marketing strategy for the next year.
She worked hard for years to reach the upper <w>echelon</w> of her chosen profession.

senses.sense_definition: A military or naval formation where units are arranged in diagonal, parallel rows.

examples.text: The fighter jets flew in a tight <w>echelon</w> during the air show display.
The general ordered the infantry to advance in an <w>echelon</w> to better cover the uneven terrain.

senses.sense_definition: A diagonal line of cyclists riding close together to reduce wind resistance.

examples.text: The peloton formed an <w>echelon</w> to protect the team leader from the strong crosswinds.
Riding in an <w>echelon</w> requires great skill and concentration to avoid crashing.

senses.sense_definition: To arrange troops or units into a diagonal, stepped formation.

examples.text: The commander began <w>echeloning</w> his forces to prepare for the upcoming defensive maneuver.
They <w>echeloned</w> the ships to maintain a clear line of sight for the artillery.

senses.sense_definition: Describing a matrix that has been processed so that the leading non-zero entries form a stepped pattern.

examples.text: The student successfully converted the system of equations into an <w>echelon</w> matrix.
Gaussian elimination is the standard method used to put a matrix into <w>echelon</w> form.

senses.sense_definition: A global signals intelligence and analysis network.

examples.text: The existence of the <w>Echelon</w> system was a subject of intense public debate in the late nineties.
Reports suggested that <w>Echelon</w> was used to intercept private satellite communications.
